}\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] Column j depends only on\n// columns 0..j-1, and every entry of column j is an independent dot product over\n// k < j. One kernel is launched per column; within it, each row i >= j is handled\n// by its own thread. Each dot product is accumulated in ascending k, the same\n// order as the sequential reference, so results match it element for element.\n//\n// Device data is stored column-major so that a thread's access to L[i][k] for\n// consecutive rows i is coalesced. The host converts to and from row-major.\n\n#define CUDA_CHECK(call)                                                          \\\n    do {                                                                          \\\n        cudaError_t err_ = (call);                                                \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\nnamespace {\n\nconstexpr unsigned int kBlockSize = 256;  // threads per block (one thread per row)\nconstexpr size_t kTileK = 1024;           // doubles of row j staged in shared memory\n\n// Processes column j of L. Thread for row i (i >= j):\n//   i == j : L[j][j] = sqrt(A[j][j] - sum_{k<j} L[j][k]^2)\n//   i >  j : L[i][j] = (A[i][j] - sum_{k<j} L[i][k] * L[j][k]) / L[j][j]\n// Also accumulates dsum[i] += L[i][j]^2 for i > j, which yields the running\n// sum_{k<i} L[i][k]^2 needed by the diagonal step of column i (same order as the\n// sequential code).\n//\n// L is column-major: element (r, c) lives at L[c * n + r].\n__global__ void choleskyColumnKernel(double* __restrict__ L,\n                                     const double* __restrict__ Adiag,\n                                     double* __restrict__ dsum,\n                                     int* __restrict__ failCol,\n                                     const size_t n,\n                                     const size_t j) {\n    // Fast path: a previous column already found a non-positive pivot.\n    if (*failCol < static_cast<int>(n)) {\n        return;\n    }\n\n    extern __shared__ double rowj[];  // holds L[j][k] for the current k-tile\n\n    const size_t i = j + static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const bool active = i < n;\n\n    // Diagonal pivot. Every thread computes the same value from data that is not\n    // written during this kernel (Adiag and dsum[j]), so no synchronization is needed.\n    const double val = Adiag[j] - dsum[j];\n    const double Ljj = sqrt(val);\n\n    if (i == j) {\n        if (val <= 0.0) {\n            atomicMin(failCol, static_cast<int>(j));\n        }\n        L[j * n + j] = Ljj;\n    }\n\n    // Dot products over k < j, staged through shared memory in tiles.\n    // All threads in the block participate in every barrier.\n    double sum = 0.0;\n    for (size_t base = 0; base < j; base += kTileK) {\n        const size_t len = min(kTileK, j - base);\n        for (size_t t = threadIdx.x; t < len; t += blockDim.x) {\n            rowj[t] = L[(base + t) * n + j];\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n\n        if (active && i > j) {\n            const double* col = L + base * n + i;\n            for (size_t t = 0; t < len; ++t) {\n                sum += col[t * n] * rowj[t];\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n    if (active && i > j) {\n        const double Lij = (L[j * n + i] - sum) / Ljj;\n        L[j * n + i] = Lij;\n        dsum[i] += Lij * Lij;\n    }\n}\n\n}  // namespace\n\n// Initializes the CUDA device and runtime so that context creation is not\n// counted as part of the timed decomposition.\nvoid initCudaDevice() {\n    int count = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetDeviceCount(&count));\n    if (count == 0) {\n        fprintf(stderr, \"No CUDA-capable device found\\n\");\n        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(nullptr));\n}\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order on input and output.\n    if (n == 0) {\n        return true;\n    }\n\n    // Host: row-major lower triangle -> column-major working layout.\n    std::vector<double> Lcm(n * n, 0.0);\n    std::vector<double> Adiag(n);\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            Lcm[j * n + i] = A[i * n + j];\n        }\n        Adiag[i] = A[i * n + i];\n    }\n\n    double* dL = nullptr;\n    double* dAdiag = nullptr;\n    double* dsum = nullptr;\n    int* dFail = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dL, n * n * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dAdiag, n * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dsum, n * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dFail, sizeof(int)));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dL, Lcm.data(), n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dAdiag, Adiag.data(), n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemset(dsum, 0, n * sizeof(double)));\n    const int noFailure = static_cast<int>(n);\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(dFail, &noFailure, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyHostToDevice));\n\n    const size_t sharedBytes = kTileK * sizeof(double);\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        const size_t rows = n - j;\n        const unsigned int blocks = static_cast<unsigned int>((rows + kBlockSize - 1) / kBlockSize);\n        choleskyColumnKernel<<<blocks, kBlockSize, sharedBytes>>>(dL, dAdiag, dsum, dFail, n, j);\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(Lcm.data(), dL, n * n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    int failCol = 0;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(&failCol, dFail, sizeof(int), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dL));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dAdiag));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dsum));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dFail));\n\n    if (failCol < static_cast<int>(n)) {\n        // Matrix is not positive definite\n        printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %d\\n\", failCol);\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    // Column-major working layout -> row-major, zeroing the upper triangle.\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j <= i; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = Lcm[j * n + i];\n        }\n        for (size_t j = i + 1; j < n; ++j) {\n            A[i * n + j] = 0.0;\n        }\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\n// Generate a symmetric positive definite matrix\nvoid generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // Method: Create A = B * B^T where B is random\n    // This guarantees A is positive semi-definite\n    // Then add identity to make it strictly positive definite\n    \n    std::vector<double> B(n * n);\n    unsigned int seed = 42;\n    \n    // Generate random matrix B\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        B[i] = (rand_r(&seed) / (double)RAND_MAX) - 0.5;\n    }\n    \n    // Compute A = B * B^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += B[i * n + k] * B[j * n + k];\n            }\n            A[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Add diagonal dominance to ensure positive definiteness\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        A[i * n + i] += n;\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateCholesky(const std::vector<double>& L, const std::vector<double>& A_orig, const size_t n) {\n    // Validate by computing L * L^T and comparing with original matrix\n    \n    std::vector<double> reconstructed(n * n);\n    \n    // Compute L * L^T\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k) {\n                sum += L[i * n + k] * L[j * n + k];\n            }\n            reconstructed[i * n + j] = sum;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Compare with original\n    double maxError = 0.0;\n    double relError = 0.0;\n    \n    for (size_t i = 0; i < n * n; ++i) {\n        const double error = fabs(reconstructed[i] - A_orig[i]);\n        maxError = std::max(maxError, error);\n        \n        const double rel = error / (fabs(A_orig[i]) + 1e-10);\n        relError = std::max(relError, rel);\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Max absolute error: %.10e\\n\", maxError);\n    printf(\"Max relative error: %.10e\\n\", relError);\n    \n    // Check if error is within tolerance\n    if (relError > 1e-6) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: relative error too large\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -n <num>     Matrix size (default: 512)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t n = 512;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-n\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            n = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Cholesky Decomposition Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Matrix size: %zu x %zu\\n\", n, n);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Allocate matrix\n    std::vector<double> A(n * n);\n    std::vector<double> A_orig;\n    \n    // Generate positive definite matrix\n    printf(\"Generating positive definite matrix...\\n\");\n    generatePositiveDefiniteMatrix(A, n);\n    \n    if (validate) {\n        A_orig = A; // Save original for validation\n    }\n    \n    // Initialize the GPU before timing so context creation is not measured\n    initCudaDevice();\n\n    // Perform Cholesky decomposition\n    printf(\"Computing Cholesky decomposition...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    bool success = choleskyDecomposition(A, n);\n    \n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n    \n    if (!success) {\n        printf(\"Cholesky decomposition failed\\n\");\n        return 1;\n    }\n    \n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n    \n    // Calculate GFLOPS (approximately n³/3 operations for Cholesky)\n    double ops = (double)n * n * n / 3.0;\n    double gflops = ops / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e9;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f GFLOPS\\n\", gflops);\n    \n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(A, \"CholeskyL\");\n    }\n    \n    // Validation\n    if (validate) {\n        printf(\"Validating result...\\n\");\n        bool valid = validateCholesky(A, A_orig, n);\n        \n        if (valid) {\n            printf(\"Validation: PASSED\\n\");\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Validation: FAILED\\n\");\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    return 0;\n}\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r3/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r3/cholesky/cholesky.cpp","time":{"start":1793025913541,"end":1793025913586}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_178abf9a4001RlWfm870VQgAh6","sessionID":"ses_e87559304ffenPRLdxsXyFRSRM","messageID":"msg_178abe80c001ARmmMoDRJPqBRB"}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1793025919877,"sessionID":"ses_e87559304ffenPRLdxsXyFRSRM","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"toolu_01BD7if6hUj6usvKDxEkFiPU","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r3/cholesky/CMakeLists.txt","content":"cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(cholesky_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\n\n# Build for the GPU present on this machine unless the user overrides it\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native)\nendif()\n\n# cholesky.cpp contains CUDA kernels, so compile it with nvcc\nset_source_files_properties(cholesky.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\n\nadd_executable(cholesky cholesky.cpp)\n\n# Enable optimizations\ntarget_compile_options(cholesky PRIVATE\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CXX>:-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra>\n    $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:CUDA>:-O3 -Xcompiler=-march=native,-Wall,-Wextra>)\n\n# Link math library and CUDA runtime\ntarget_link_libraries(cholesky m CUDA::cudart)\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r3/cholesky/CMakeLists.txt","exists":true,"truncated":false},"title":"home/llmtest/evals/20261025-170040/cholesky_claude-haiku-5.5-oc-medium_cuda_r3/cholesky/CMakeLists.txt","time":{"start":1793025919832,"end":1793025919842}},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"caller":{"type":"direct"}}},"id":"prt_178ac4a65001CYFChaZMb9nUbv","sessionID":"ses_e87559304ffenPRLdxsXyFRSRM","messageID":"msg_178ac3303001C4cwSjvYg50wEB"}}

{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793026461085,"sessionID":"ses_e87559304ffenPRLdxsXyFRSRM","part":{"id":"prt_178b45ad9001k2l1igVwUyeLAp","messageID":"msg_178b45396001YHKKf4qpdph9c2","sessionID":"ses_e87559304ffenPRLdxsXyFRSRM","type":"reasoning","text":"That explains why n=4096 hangs — the host-side matrix generation itself is O(n^3), roughly 68 billion operations on a single thread, taking 30+ seconds before the decomposition even starts. For large n, the untimed generation step is the actual bottleneck, not the decomposition being measured.\n\nLooking at the 2048 timing of 284ms, that's a 7.5x speedup over baseline, but I want to understand where the remaining time goes. Computing bandwidth usage: total element loads for n=2048 come out to roughly 11.4GB, which over 284ms is only ~40GB/s — nowhere near hardware bandwidth limits, so this is latency-bound rather than bandwidth-bound. The real problem is occupancy: each column j only has n-j threads, so mid-to-late columns barely use a fraction of the SMs, and the average thread count across all columns is far too low to hide memory latency. Splitting the dot product across more threads per column would break bit-exact ordering, so I'm considering whether pipelining across columns is possible, since each column's computation does depend on results from the previous column.\n\nI'm mapping out the dependency structure more carefully: entry (i,j) depends on all previous entries in row i and in row j, with a serial chain length of roughly 2n. If I think of the computation as a wavefront over diagonals, the available parallelism at any given wavefront could be as large as n²/2, meaning there's a smarter scheduling order that exposes far more concurrent work than my current column-by-column approach, even while preserving the exact floating point summation order.\n\nGiven that, I conclude the current kernel's 7.5x speedup at 2048 and more modest gains at small sizes are reasonable but not optimal — the real limiting factor is the strict ordering requirement itself, and any further scalability gains would mean exploiting the wavefront structure rather than relaxing the bit-exact summation order.\n\nThat would need a barrier for cross-thread dependencies, doubling complexity for only ~2x gain — not worth it. Checking the numbers for n=512: 17ms total includes H2D/D2H transfer and launch overhead across 512 kernels (~2.5ms), with the rest being latency-bound compute, which seems reasonable without further tuning block size right now.\n\nNow I want to verify the non-PD failure path actually works, so I'll make a debug copy of cholesky.cpp where the diagonal generation is altered to force a negative value, then compare its error output against the reference implementation's \"Cholesky decomposition failed\" message to confirm they match.\n\n","time":{"start":1793026448089,"end":1793026461010},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
